title: First recordings with the Quality Serenaders
summary: His first records were for Victor in 1929 with the Quality Serenaders, including Charlie's Idea by Charlie Lawrence.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: You mentioned that your first recordings were around 1930. Who were the first ones with? Was it Paul Howard or Louis Armstrong?

Well, the first recordings I would say were around '29 because Louis didn't come here until '30. And it was around '29 and we were -- I was in this band called Quality Serenaders. And we had a contract with Victor. We made about -- what was it -- six, or eight, or ten records
with Victor. That was the first time I had recorded.
And all of those were with Quality Serenaders?
Yes, that was the only band I played with or made any records with besides Louis Lewis out here.
I found a reference in a book to "Charlie's Idea": A series of variations on the chords of "Tiger Rag". Was that one of the ones you made with the Quality Serenaders?

Yes. Yes. That was one of them. Now, this Charlie was incidentally Charlie Lawrence, and Charlie Lawrence was one of the men in the band that when I was in school, I used to slip over from Pasadena to come over here and here. And I was playing with Charlie Lawrence in this band of the Quality Serenaders?
